summary: Feed s161_triple to IDS is degraded: 3 faults detected - 91% encrypted traffic exceeds IDS tolerance, 10.8% jumbo frames dropped by 1518B IDS port, and 17.4% duplicates waste capacity. IDS has blind spots on encrypted and oversize flows and reduced detection efficiency.

findings.root_cause: 91.2% of bytes are encrypted (threshold 60% for this IDS). Traffic is predominantly TLS/encrypted and is being sent to IDS without prior decryption - packet broker is mirroring encrypted flows directly to IDS.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload for signature and anomaly detection but cannot inspect encrypted payloads. 91% of traffic is opaque, so IDS will miss intrusions, malware, and C2 inside TLS and will waste cycles attempting inspection.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs cleartext to detect threats. Decrypt once before IDS (or selectively forward decrypted copy) brings encrypted share below 60% tolerance while preserving privacy/policy controls.

findings.root_cause: 347 of 3224 frames (10.8%) exceed the IDS port MTU of 1518 bytes, largest 8058 bytes. Indicates jumbo frames or encapsulated traffic (e.g., VXLAN/GRE with large MTU) from network being forwarded unchanged to a 1Gbps IDS port that only supports standard Ethernet MTU.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC drops all frames >1518 bytes silently. 10.8% of traffic never reaches detection engine, creating complete blind spot for large flows - attackers can evade detection using large frames, and IDS misses attacks in those flows.

recommended_fix.why: Either enable 9000+ byte jumbo MTU on IDS port/NIC to accept 8058B frames, or configure packet broker to truncate/slice or fragment oversize frames to 1518B before delivery. Jumbo enable is preferred since IDS needs full payload.

findings.root_cause: 562 of 3224 packets (17.4%) are duplicates, well above 5% threshold. Classic packet broker aggregation issue - same packet arriving via multiple SPAN/TAP paths or both sides of a link aggregated without deduplication enabled.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes ~17% of its 1Gbps budget re-processing identical packets, inflates event counts, can skew stream reassembly and cause false positives, and reduces headroom for real traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Enable broker-level deduplication (time-window based) to suppress duplicate copies before IDS, freeing capacity and ensuring accurate detection without double-counting.
